lesson_scope: Integration of linear momentum conservation and impulse with multi-phase kinematics and dynamics; vertical free-fall and projectile motion before or after direct collision; motion down smooth or rough inclined planes linked to horizontal collisions; deceleration under friction following inelastic impacts; impulsive string jerks and sudden tension changes in connected systems.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 1: Free fall before horizontal collision

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Free fall before horizontal collision

hints: Use $v^2 = 2gs$ with $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $s = 1.8\text{ m}$ to find the speed of impact.
The impulse is equal to the change in momentum: $I = m \Delta v = 0.2 \times 6.0\text{ N s}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate impact speed using constant acceleration under gravity:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2gs = 0^2 + 2(10)(1.8) = 36$$
$$v = \sqrt{36} = 6.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the magnitude of the impulse:
$$I = |m(v_f - v_i)| = |0.2(0 - 6.0)| = 1.2\text{ N s}$$
The floor exerts an upward impulse of $1.2\text{ N s}$ on the particle.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Kinematics of vertical drop:
$$v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2(10)(1.8)} = 6.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Compute impulse from momentum change:
$$I = \Delta p = 0.2 \times 6.0 = 1.2\text{ N s}$$
Directed vertically upwards against gravity and motion.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies vertical free-fall kinematics: $v^2 = u^2 + 2gs = 0 + 2(10)(1.8) = 36 \implies v = 6.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculates impulse exerted by floor: $I = |\Delta p| = 0.2(6.0 - 0) = 1.2\text{ N s}$ directed upwards.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 2: Coalescence followed by deceleration on a rough horizontal surface

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 2: Coalescence followed by deceleration on a rough horizontal surface

hints: Conserve linear momentum during coalescence: $0.3 \times 4 = 0.8 v_C$.
Frictional deceleration on a horizontal plane is $a = \mu g = 0.15 \times 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply conservation of linear momentum across the collision:
$$m_A u_A = (m_A + m_B) v_C$$
$$0.3(4) = (0.3 + 0.5) v_C \implies 1.2 = 0.8 v_C \implies v_C = \frac{1.2}{0.8} = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the decelerating combined particle:
$$R = m_C g, \quad F_r = \mu R = \mu m_C g$$
$$m_C a = F_r \implies a = \mu g = 0.15 \times 10 = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine common speed:
$$v_C = \frac{0.3 \times 4}{0.8} = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Compute frictional deceleration:
$$a = \mu g = 0.15(10) = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Mass cancels out when determining sliding deceleration on a horizontal level.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies momentum conservation during coalescence: $0.3(4) = (0.3 + 0.5) v_C \implies 1.2 = 0.8 v_C \implies v_C = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Applies Newton's second law on rough surface: $F_r = \mu m_C g \implies m_C a = \mu m_C g \implies a = \mu g = 0.15(10) = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 6: Time to come to rest after an impulsive impact

hints: Find initial speed $u = \frac{I}{m} = \frac{3.0}{0.5} = 6.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate initial speed and deceleration:
$$u = \frac{I}{m} = \frac{3.0}{0.5} = 6.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$a = \frac{F_r}{m} = \frac{2.0}{0.5} = 4.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

$$v = u - at \implies 0 = 6.0 - 4.0 t \implies t = \frac{6.0}{4.0} = 1.5\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Use impulse-momentum relation directly:
$$F_r t = I = \Delta p$$
$$2.0 t = 3.0$$

Solve for duration:
$$t = \frac{3.0}{2.0} = 1.5\text{ s}$$
Friction dissipates the entire momentum in $1.5\text{ s}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Finds initial speed from impulse: $I = m u \implies 3.0 = 0.5 u \implies u = 6.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and deceleration $a = \frac{F}{m} = \frac{2.0}{0.5} = 4.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (or applies $I_{\text{friction}} = F t = m u$).
Evaluates time to rest: $v = u - at \implies 0 = 6.0 - 4.0 t \implies t = 1.5\text{ s}$ (or $t = \frac{3.0}{2.0} = 1.5\text{ s}$).

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Problem 5: Mid-air collision of vertically projected particles

hints: Take upwards as positive: $u_A = +10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $u_B = -10\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Conserve momentum: $0.2(10) + 0.3(-10) = 0.5 v_C$ to find $v_C$.
Notice the sign of $v_C$: since $v_C = -2.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the combined body moves downwards immediately after impact.
The collision occurs at height $y = 20(1) - 5(1^2) = 15\text{ m}$, which is its maximum height.

walkthrough.text:
Apply conservation of linear momentum taking upwards as positive:
$$m_A u_A + m_B u_B = (m_A + m_B) v_C$$
$$0.2(+10.0) + 0.3(-10.0) = (0.2 + 0.3) v_C$$
$$2.0 - 3.0 = 0.5 v_C$$
$$-1.0 = 0.5 v_C \implies v_C = -2.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The combined particle moves downwards with speed $2.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Determine the greatest height reached above the ground:
The height of the collision point above ground is:
$$y_{\text{collision}} = 20(1.0) - 5(1.0^2) = 15.0\text{ m}$$
Since the combined particle has a downward velocity immediately after impact ($v_C < 0$), it never ascends above the point of impact.
Therefore, the greatest height above the ground reached by the combined particle is $15.0\text{ m}$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Compute coalesced velocity:
$$v_C = \frac{0.2(+10) + 0.3(-10)}{0.5} = \frac{-1.0}{0.5} = -2.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Downwards momentum dominates.

Evaluate apex height:
$$y = 20(1) - 5(1^2) = 15.0\text{ m}$$
Because velocity points downwards post-collision, no further ascent occurs; maximum height is identically $15.0\text{ m}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies conservation of linear momentum with vertical directions: $0.2(10) + 0.3(-10) = (0.2 + 0.3) v_C$.
Evaluates common velocity: $2.0 - 3.0 = 0.5 v_C \implies 0.5 v_C = -1.0 \implies v_C = -2.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (speed $2.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ downwards).
Finds height of collision $y = 20(1.0) - 5(1.0^2) = 15.0\text{ m}$, and notes that since $v_C$ is directed downwards, the greatest height reached is the collision height $15.0\text{ m}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Problem 6: Particle accelerated on rough incline followed by horizontal collision and braking

hints: Resolve perpendicular to the incline: $R = m g\cos\alpha = 0.5 \times 10 \times 0.8 = 4.0\text{ N}$.
Find the frictional resistance: $F_r = \mu_1 R = 0.25 \times 4.0 = 1.0\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law up the slope: $6.0 - 1.0 - 0.5(10)(0.6) = 0.5 a$, giving $a = 4.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Use $v^2 = 2as = 2(4.0)(2.5) = 20$ to find the speed at the top of the incline.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane and calculate friction:
$$R = m_A g \cos\alpha = 0.5(10)(0.8) = 4.0\text{ N}$$
$$F_r = \mu_1 R = 0.25(4.0) = 1.0\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law parallel to the plane:
$$P - m_A g \sin\alpha - F_r = m_A a$$
$$6.0 - 0.5(10)(0.6) - 1.0 = 0.5 a$$
$$6.0 - 3.0 - 1.0 = 0.5 a \implies 2.0 = 0.5 a \implies a = 4.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Calculate the speed at the top:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as = 0 + 2(4.0)(2.5) = 20 \implies v = \sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5} \approx 4.47\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Normal reaction and friction:
$$R = 0.5(10)(0.8) = 4.0\text{ N}, \quad F_r = 0.25(4.0) = 1.0\text{ N}$$

Dynamics and incline exit velocity:
$$a = \frac{6.0 - 3.0 - 1.0}{0.5} = 4.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
$$v = \sqrt{2(4.0)(2.5)} = \sqrt{20} \approx 4.47\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Block $A$ reaches the crest with speed $\sqrt{20}\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves forces perpendicular to incline and finds friction: $R = m_A g\cos\alpha = 0.5(10)(0.8) = 4.0\text{ N} \implies F_r = \mu_1 R = 0.25(4.0) = 1.0\text{ N}$.
Applies Newton's second law parallel to incline: $P - F_r - m_A g\sin\alpha = m_A a \implies 6.0 - 1.0 - 0.5(10)(0.6) = 0.5 a \implies 2.0 = 0.5 a \implies a = 4.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Applies $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 0$, $a = 4.0$, and $s = 2.5$: $v^2 = 2(4.0)(2.5) = 20 \implies v = \sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5} \approx 4.47\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Problem 6: Particle accelerated on rough incline followed by horizontal collision and braking

hints: Total momentum before horizontal impact is $m_A v_A = 0.5 \times \sqrt{20}$.
After coalescing, the combined mass is $0.5 + 0.5 = 1.0\text{ kg}$.
Equate initial and final momentum: $0.5\sqrt{20} = 1.0 v_C$.
Simplify: $v_C = \frac{\sqrt{20}}{2} = \sqrt{5} \approx 2.24\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Conserve linear momentum across the horizontal coalescence:
$$m_A v_A + m_B(0) = (m_A + m_B) v_C$$
$$0.5(\sqrt{20}) = (0.5 + 0.5) v_C$$
$$1.0 v_C = 0.5\sqrt{20}$$

Simplify to find the common speed $v_C$:
$$v_C = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{20} = \sqrt{\frac{20}{4}} = \sqrt{5} \approx 2.24\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Equate momentum:
$$p_i = 0.5\sqrt{20}\text{ N s}$$
$$p_f = 1.0 v_C$$

Solve for speed:
$$v_C = \frac{0.5\sqrt{20}}{1.0} = \sqrt{5} \approx 2.24\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Velocity halves upon coalescing with an identical resting mass.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies conservation of linear momentum to the horizontal collision: $0.5(\sqrt{20}) = (0.5 + 0.5) v_C$.
Evaluates speed of $C$: $v_C = \frac{\sqrt{20}}{2} = \sqrt{5} \approx 2.24\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Problem 6: Particle accelerated on rough incline followed by horizontal collision and braking

hints: Normal reaction on the horizontal plane is $R = 1.0 \times 10 = 10\text{ N}$.
Frictional resistance is $F_r = \mu_2 R = 0.2 \times 10 = 2.0\text{ N}$, so deceleration is $a = 2.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Use $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = \sqrt{5}\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v = 0$.
Solve $0 = 5 - 4 s$ to get $s = 1.25\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate normal reaction and friction on the horizontal plane:
$$R = m_C g = 1.0 \times 10 = 10\text{ N}$$
$$F_r = \mu_2 R = 0.2 \times 10 = 2.0\text{ N}$$
$$a_C = \frac{F_r}{m_C} = \frac{2.0}{1.0} = 2.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate the stopping distance:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$$
$$0 = (\sqrt{5})^2 - 2(2.0)s$$
$$0 = 5 - 4.0 s \implies s = \frac{5}{4} = 1.25\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Calculate frictional deceleration:
$$a = \mu_2 g = 0.2(10) = 2.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply work-energy / kinematics:
$$s = \frac{v_C^2}{2a} = \frac{5}{2(2.0)} = 1.25\text{ m}$$
The coalesced block halts after $1.25\text{ m}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Finds deceleration of $C$: $F_r = \mu_2(m_C g) = 0.2(1.0 \times 10) = 2.0\text{ N} \implies a = \frac{2.0}{1.0} = 2.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Applies $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u^2 = (\sqrt{5})^2 = 5$ and $v = 0$: $0 = 5 - 2(2.0)s \implies 4.0 s = 5.0 \implies s = 1.25\text{ m}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Problem 7: Two-particle vertical drop with string jerk and bounce impact

hints: Use $v^2 = 2gh$ with $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $h = 1.2\text{ m}$ to find the speed of $P$ just as the string tightens.
Calculate $v = \sqrt{2(10)(1.2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
The impulsive jerk in the string acts internally between $P$ and $Q$. Conserve vertical linear momentum: $m_P v = (m_P + m_Q) v_{\text{common}}$.
Substitute $0.4\sqrt{24} = 1.0 v_{\text{common}}$, yielding $v_{\text{common}} = 0.4\sqrt{24} \approx 1.96\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the speed of $P$ immediately before the string becomes taut:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2gh = 0^2 + 2(10)(1.2) = 24$$
$$v = \sqrt{24} = 2\sqrt{6} \approx 4.90\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Apply conservation of vertical linear momentum during the jerk:
$$m_P v + m_Q(0) = (m_P + m_Q) v_{\text{common}}$$
$$0.4(\sqrt{24}) = (0.4 + 0.6) v_{\text{common}}$$
$$v_{\text{common}} = \frac{0.4\sqrt{24}}{1.0} = 0.4(2\sqrt{6}) = \frac{4\sqrt{6}}{5} \approx 1.96\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Free fall of $P$:
$$v_P = \sqrt{2(10)(1.2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Impulsive tension jerk:
$$v_{\text{common}} = \frac{m_P v_P}{m_P + m_Q} = \frac{0.4\sqrt{24}}{1.0} = 0.4\sqrt{24} \approx 1.96\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Vertical momentum transfers into the combined two-particle system.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies free-fall kinematics to $P$: $v^2 = 2gh = 2(10)(1.2) = 24$.
Obtains speed of $P$ immediately before string jerks: $v = \sqrt{24} = 2\sqrt{6} \approx 4.90\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Applies conservation of linear momentum to the impulsive jerk in the vertical direction: $m_P v = (m_P + m_Q) v_{\text{common}}$.
Evaluates common speed: $0.4(\sqrt{24}) = (0.4 + 0.6) v_{\text{common}} \implies v_{\text{common}} = 0.4\sqrt{24} = \frac{4\sqrt{6}}{5} \approx 1.96\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

hints: Impulse on $Q$ is its gain in momentum: $I = m_Q v_{\text{common}} = 0.6 \times (0.4\sqrt{24}) = 0.24\sqrt{24} \approx 1.18\text{ N s}$.

Kinetic energy immediately after jerk: $KE_f = \frac{1}{2}(m_P + m_Q) v_{\text{common}}^2 = \frac{1}{2}(1.0)(1.9596^2) = 1.92\text{ J}$.

$$I = m_Q(v_{\text{common}} - 0) = 0.6(0.4\sqrt{24}) = 0.24\sqrt{24} \approx 1.18\text{ N s}$$

Calculate the kinetic energies before and after the string becomes taut:
$$KE_i = \frac{1}{2}m_P v^2 = \frac{1}{2}(0.4)(24) = 4.8\text{ J}$$
$$KE_f = \frac{1}{2}(m_P + m_Q) v_{\text{common}}^2 = \frac{1}{2}(1.0)(0.4^2 \times 24) = 0.5 \times 3.84 = 1.92\text{ J}$$

Mechanical energy loss during inelastic jerk:
$$KE_i = 4.8\text{ J}, \quad KE_f = 1.92\text{ J}$$
$$\Delta E = 4.8 - 1.92 = 2.88\text{ J}$$
$60\%$ of the kinetic energy is dissipated instantaneously when the string snaps taut.
